page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs based on the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 12 physical cores and 1 thread per core. It includes 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8800.46 and a PassMark CPU score of 10233.84. However, single-core capabilities are relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.38 and a poor single-threaded gzip compression rate of 19.09 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is moderate, reaching 492.04 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 59.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations and Redis SET performance are average, with Redis handling 8.46 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.sn1ne.3xlarge is its low memory-to-CPU ratio and weak single-threaded performance, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications or single-core bottlenecked tasks. However, its dedicated physical cores and average multi-threaded performance make it a cost-efficient option for parallelized compute workloads that do not require local storage. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded batch processing, moderate database operations, and lightweight web serving.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU resources. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 10233.84 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 43.18 GB/sec, contrasted by weak single-core performance. Memory bandwidth is moderate, supporting up to 492.04 GB/sec for cached reads. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for parallelized, compute-bound workloads that do not demand high memory density or local disk storage. It is best suited for multi-threaded batch processing, moderate database operations, and distributed computing tasks.
